transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello. Nice to meet you too. Well, I came in because I just can’t seem to keep my mind on things the way I used to. I'm a loan officer, and lately I'll just stare at a loan worksheet or a client follow-up list, and I end up rereading the same line over and over again. And then I just put off making my calls. It feels like even simple decisions are a lot harder than they should be right now.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yes, I suppose I have. Most days, there's just this... dull heaviness that kind of sits with me. Even when I go to the community center or spend time out in my garden—places that used to really lift my spirits—it doesn't help much anymore. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? Just pasting a smile on and getting through the day.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Well, like I was saying about the garden and the community center... I guess I haven't completely lost interest, because I still go and try to do those things. But the pleasure just isn't really there. I don't get that same good feeling out of them anymore.
How have you been sleeping lately?
My sleep has been pretty normal, actually. I haven't really noticed any changes there. I usually go to bed around the same time and wake up around the same time, and I sleep through the night fine.
Before this current period, have you ever had another stretch in your life when you felt depressed like this?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had sad days like anyone else, but nothing that lasted this long or felt quite like this steady... heaviness. This is really the first time it's been like this.
When you were a child, did you often have trouble paying attention or staying focused?

No, not that I remember. I... I always did fine in school, as far as paying attention and getting my work done goes. So, no, I don't think I ever had trouble focusing as a child. It was never really an issue for me back then.
Did these problems start after something stressful happened in your life?
Yes, it did. Um, this has been going on since... well, since my close friend died. That was a little over two years ago now. So, yes, that's really when all this started.
Do you find yourself feeling a strong sense of longing for your friend who died?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, of course I miss her, but... I don't really have that strong sense of longing you're talking about. It's not like I'm constantly yearning for her or anything like that. It's more just that... well, this heavy feeling settled in after she passed, and it just hasn't gone away.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things?

No, not really. I mean, I worry about normal things, like anyone else... but it's not excessive. I don't sit around worrying about a million different things all day. It's really just this... this constant low mood that I can't shake, not anxiety.
Have you felt this low mood nearly every day for the past two years?

Yes, I'd say so. Most days there's just this dull heaviness sitting with me. Even when I'm out at the community center or working in my garden... places that really used to lift me up... I just feel like I'm going through the motions. I'll have a smile pasted on, but that heavy feeling is still right there. So, yes, it's been nearly every day.
Do you often feel hopeless?

Yes, I suppose I do. I keep telling myself that things might turn around eventually, but... underneath that, I just have this really tired feeling. It feels like this is just how my life is going to be now—just smaller and harder, no matter what I try to do.
During these past two years, was there ever a period of at least two weeks when your depression felt noticeably worse than usual?

No, I don't think so. It doesn't really fluctuate like that. It's just... consistently there. I haven't noticed a time where it suddenly got a lot worse for a couple of weeks. It's really just the same steady heaviness day in and day out.
